key_insight: Neural networks can end up behaving similarly on the same final task while still carrying measurable internal traces of earlier training history.
engineering_relevance: For constitutive and AI surrogate modeling, this means matching accuracy alone may not guarantee identical internal state evolution or transfer behavior across training protocols.
method: Paired CNNs started from identical weights
Task order was reversed, then both models underwent the same deterministic common-relaxation training
Controls tested longer relaxation, rotated-MNIST, and activation-function differences
evidence_signal: Across 20 paired MNIST runs, 16 met behavioral matching but still showed a mean representation-history score of 0.139 and about 3.1% prediction disagreement; the effect persisted through 50,000 updates.
watch_item: These findings are protocol-scoped, so conclusions may not generalize beyond the specific architectures, datasets, and training schedules tested.
paper_title: Behavioral Convergence Without Representational Convergence: Persistent Training-History Dependence in Neural Networks
